answer: When k identities coordinate equivocation, verifiable links among their signed messages trigger a joint penalty proportional to k², deducted from bonded collateral escrows rather than assessed as isolated faults. Sybil operators cannot dilute exposure by splitting stake: detection applies asymmetric capital depreciation, compounding an exponential loss multiplier across the controlled swarm. Thus quill, forge, and comet identities acting together face greater expected loss than independent validators.
